thread.title: HP Still Tops in PCs: Companies Stock Up, China Declines

author: Tiernan Ray
title: HP Still Tops in PCs: Companies Stock Up, China Declines
text:
By Tiernan Ray Updated April 11, 2018 5:11 p.m. ET Research firms Gartner and IDC just released their personal computer data for Q1, and the results were sales that were either flat with, or down slightly, from a year earlier, depending on whom you believe.
Illustration: iStockphoto HP ( HPQ ) was still in first place, while Apple ( AAPL ) recorded minimal sales growth but stayed in fourth place, with a 6.9% share.
Gartner says PCs dropped by 1.4%, year over year. IDC says they were exactly flat.
Gartner and IDC have very different attitudes about the results: IDC notes this is the third quarter in a row with PC shipment volume being about flat. Gartner calls it the "14th consecutive quarter of decline, dating back to the second quarter of 2012."
IDC is fairly upbeat, saying the U.S. market had a “promising opening quarter” and that the market overall is proving “resilient.” The firm ties this to the “continued build up in commercial renewal” that was “stabilizing” the market.
Gartner notes that PCs in China dropped 5.7%, the “major contributor” to the overall market decline.
Privately held Dell had the biggest gains for the quarter, seeing a roughly 6.5% rise in shipments, year over year, while staying in third place, according to both firms. HP came in ahead of Lenovo Group ( 0992.Hong Kong ), and IDC gives HP a little bit more robust growth, at 4.3%, versus the mere 2.8% recorded by Gartner.
Apple’s 6.9% share, according to Gartner, was up slightly from a 6.7% share a year earlier, while IDC has Apple in fifth place behind Taiwan’s Acer ( 2353.Taiwan ). IDC has Apple shipments dropping by 4.8% year over year, while Gartner says Apple shipments rose by 1.5%.
